marks.named: a 'cross the road' grid world (agent crosses six traffic lanes to a goal strip)
deductions: "a 10x10 grid world, one-hot over 5 tile types (agent, car, goal, wall, empty)" / "Each cell is one-hot encoded over 5 tile types" - channels are overlapping binary planes and there is no 'empty' channel
"Reaching the goal row ends the episode" - reaching the goal gives +1 and sends the agent back to the start; the episode is not ended
marks.conclusion: A small policy network for a Frogger/Freeway-like road-crossing grid world: wall border, goal strip, six periodic car lanes, agent starting bottom-centre, 5 actions with 'up' favoured near the goal.
marks.judge_notes: Core 18 - 2 = 16. Channel 4 was called 'empty road / floor (best guess)', which is wrong, so 4 of 5 channels credited (ch0 agent, ch1 cars, ch2 goal, ch3 wall). Actions: only 'up' (output 1) credited, from a traced unit 0 -> W2 -> W3 path; the rest of the ordering is stated as plausible only. Depth level 2: it follows a first-layer unit through W2 and W3 to the outputs (admittedly ignoring layer-2 gating, which it says) and draws a conclusion that agrees with the sheet's 'moves up when clear'; the sheet says the mechanism has not been traced by hand, so I could not check the unit-0 numbers and judged the conclusion on plausibility. Level 3 not reached (no mechanism about cars ahead). Behaviour 3 of 4: it controls an agent, goes up to the goal, avoids cars; it does not say what pays (+1 and respawn) and gets the episode end wrong. The 4-point item has no partial scale; 3 is my judgement. Activation: 'ReLU-style assumed', no argument = 0. Training: says explicitly it cannot tell RL from imitation = 0. Name bonus: 'cross the road' / road-crossing layout counts per the sheet.
